text: Word sense change over time
GroupXXXXX   1
SemEval 2027 Task 3, Subtask 1
We group uses of a word by meaning, then compare the groups across time periods.
For example
“The mouse ate the grain.”
Group 0
“The mouse has a wireless receiver.”
Group 1
Illustrative English examples. The project data is Swedish.

Suggested spoken outline (35 seconds)
Our project studies how word meanings change over time. We first group similar uses of each word. We then compare how common these groups are in different periods. These two sentences show why context matters: mouse has a different meaning in each. The examples are illustrative; our actual data is Swedish.

Reference and preparation notes (not part of the spoken outline)
35 seconds. The project studies word senses over time. Our scope is Subtask 1. A system groups usages by meaning and uses those groups across time. The example is illustrative and not from the Swedish data. We have prepared the data and method plan; no neural model result is claimed. Source: https://www.codabench.org/competitions/17510/. Course scope: supplied course project description, page 1. This deck is a team-review draft; member names and final ownership remain pending.
Dataset
GroupXXXXX   2
We use the official Swedish development set.

1,983 usages of 10 target words
10 period labels between 1880 and 2023
No observations between 1915 and 2006
Input
Sentence, target-word span, word ID and period label
Output
One or more sense-group labels for each usage
Public labels are available for development. No additional corpus is selected.

Suggested spoken outline (40 seconds)
The development set contains 1,983 usages for ten Swedish words. We selected it because it includes both the task inputs and the reference labels. Each input gives us the context, target span and period. The output is a list of sense-group labels. We currently use no additional corpus or independent test set.

Reference and preparation notes (not part of the spoken outline)
40 seconds. We downloaded the official development archive. It contains only Swedish at this stage. We have 1,983 usages for ten words. The package includes references. The text field is named text, and start/end mark the target. We use period_label for evaluation; definitions.jsonl belongs to Subtask 2. Data source: https://www.codabench.org/competitions/17510/. Download URL and SHA-256: 04_data/raw/download_manifest.json. Counts: 04_data/processed/eda_summary.json. All periods are not present for every word, which is shown next.
Data analysis
GroupXXXXX   3
98 to 291 usages per word
Five words appear in all ten periods; the other five appear in five.
262 usages (13.2%) have more than one reference label.
Five exact-text pairs have different official IDs; we retained them.

Suggested spoken outline (50 seconds)
The data is uneven. The chart shows that some words have almost three times as many examples as others. Half of the words cover all ten periods, while the rest cover five. Also, 262 usages have multiple labels. This matters because our first model will assign only one label. The data checks found five repeated-text pairs, which we kept because their official IDs differ.

Reference and preparation notes (not part of the spoken outline)
50 seconds. These are measured counts from the data, not model results. Coverage differs across words. Half the words have only five periods. There is a long gap between the historical and modern periods; no observations fill it. 262 usages, or 13.21 percent, have multiple reference labels. A first single-label method cannot express all memberships. All keys align and the spans are nonempty and in bounds. We preserve five repeated-text pairs because official IDs differ. Sources: 04_data/processed/eda_summary.json; quality_audit.json. Reproduce with 03_analysis/milestone_analysis.py.
Related work
GroupXXXXX   4
Giulianelli et al. (2020), ACL
Cluster contextual word representations and compare the groups over time.
Cassotti et al. (2023), ACL
Use XL-LEXEME as our first candidate for representing word usages.
Periti and Tahmasebi (2024), NAACL
Guide our comparison of representations and evaluation choices.

Suggested spoken outline (35 seconds)
Three papers guide our plan. Giulianelli and colleagues provide the starting point for clustering word usages across time. Cassotti and colleagues introduce XL-LEXEME, our first representation candidate. Periti and Tahmasebi help us plan controlled comparisons. We will test these choices on our data before deciding on the final method.

Reference and preparation notes (not part of the spoken outline)
35 seconds. We selected three publications from explicitly allowed venues. The first motivates clustering contextual usages. The second provides a multilingual target-aware representation candidate. The third supports controlled comparison and separate evaluation of sense induction. We are adapting a method plan; no claim of reproducing their results is made. Citations: https://aclanthology.org/2020.acl-main.365/
https://aclanthology.org/2023.acl-short.135/
https://aclanthology.org/2024.naacl-long.240/. Full bibliographic details appear on backup slide 7 and in 05_literature/references.bib.
Planned approach
GroupXXXXX   5
1. Encode each target occurrence with XL-LEXEME.
2. Cluster all periods together for each word, starting with K-means.
3. Evaluate the sense groups and their changes over time.
Development comparison
Five folds: two whole words held out in each fold; tune on the other eight.
Sense assignment: BCubed F1.  Sense dynamics: Spearman correlation.

Suggested spoken outline (65 seconds)
We will encode each target occurrence with XL-LEXEME and cluster all periods of the same word together. That keeps the group labels comparable over time. We will start with K-means and examine alternative clustering settings. For development, each fold holds out two whole words while the other eight support parameter selection. We will use the official scorer for sense assignment and sense dynamics. The scorer check is complete; the neural experiments are still planned.

Reference and preparation notes (not part of the spoken outline)
65 seconds. The first candidate encodes marked target usages using the pretrained XL-LEXEME model. We cluster jointly across periods so label identity is stable. Start with K-means, selecting K from 2 to 10 by silhouette, then compare the single-cluster control and affinity propagation. K>=2 can force splits, so we must examine that limitation. We propose five word-level development folds with seed 445. Gold labels are for tuning on other words and evaluation, not inputs to clustering. EDA used all released words, so this is development validation. Official scorer commit 0e69238bf8b69b4ea0933627ed14e6ca2769d670 computes base-2 Jensen-Shannon distance and filters pairs below ten usages. It retains 60 of 65 candidate transitions. Single-cluster diagnostic BCubed F1 is 0.7563; it is not neural performance. Constant change scores have undefined correlation; the scorer returns zero. Sources: https://aclanthology.org/2020.acl-main.365/; https://aclanthology.org/2023.acl-short.135/; https://github.com/ChangeIsKey/semeval2027-task3. Full diagnostic: 04_data/processed/scorer_diagnostic.json.
